'''Aaron R. Parsons''' (born 1980) is an American [[astrophysicist]] who works primarily in the fields of [[radio astronomy]] instrumentation and experimental [[Physical cosmology|cosmology]].

== Biography ==
{{BLP one source|section|date=September 2021}}
Parsons was born in 1980.  He grew up in [[Rangely, Colorado]] and graduated simultaneously from high school and from [[Colorado Northwestern Community College]] with an [[Associate of Science|AS]] degree in 1998.  He majored in [[physics]] and [[mathematics]] at [[Harvard University]], and graduated with a [[Bachelor of Arts|BA]] in 2002.
After working as a development engineer at the [[Space Sciences Laboratory|UC Berkeley Space Sciences Lab]] from 2002 to 2004, Parsons entered graduate school at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in [[astronomy]], receiving his [[PhD]] in 2009 while holding a predoctoral research position at [[Arecibo Observatory]] in Puerto Rico.  Parsons returned to UC Berkeley on an [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] postdoctoral fellowship in 2009.  He was hired as an assistant [[professor]] in the Astronomy Department and in the [[Radio Astronomy Laboratory]] at UC Berkeley in 2011.<ref name="UC Berkeley Astronomy Faculty">{{cite web |url = http://astro.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/parsons.html |title = UC Berkeley Astronomy Department Faculty: Aaron Parsons |author = Regents of UC Berkeley |year = 2011 |access-date = 2012-11-23 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120323142751/http://astro.berkeley.edu/people/faculty/parsons.html |archive-date = 2012-03-23 |url-status = dead }}</ref>

== Research ==
Parsons is the [[principal investigator]] of the [[Hydrogen Epoch of Reionization Array]] and the [[Precision Array for Probing the Epoch of Reionization]] (PAPER) array, a radio interferometer designed to detect the first era of star formation, commonly called the [[Epoch of Reionization]], via its effect on hydrogen in the [[intergalactic medium]].<ref name="NSF PAPER">{{cite web | url = https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1129258 | title = National Science Foundation: Collaborative Research: Precision Array for Probing the Epoch of Reionization (PAPER) | author =National Science Foundation | year = 2011 | access-date = 2012-11-23}}</ref>  He specializes in digital signal processing instrumentation, and was one of the founding members of the Center for Astronomy Signal Processing and Electronics Research (CASPER).<ref name="CASPER">{{cite web | url = https://casper.berkeley.edu/wiki/CASPER_Advisory_Board | title = CASPER Advisory Board | author = Regents of UC Berkeley | date = November 2010 | access-date = 2012-11-23 }}</ref>

== Creative Works ==

===''Coherence'' (2025)===
Parsons published his first book, the novel ''Coherence'', on December 8, 2025 with EoR Publishing.<ref>{{cite book | last1=Parsons | first1=Aaron | title=Coherence | date=8 December 2025 | publisher=EoR | isbn=979-8-9934114-0-8 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Xhem0QEACAAJ }}</ref> The book follows the protagonist Ruby, a graduate student in a Boston-area physics program, as she navigates a web of lies woven by humans and an artificially intelligent agent dubbed MiddleMan. As the lies compound, she is drawn into conflict with her advisor Mendel, her boyfriend Noah, and the exploitative systems surrounding her. Noah, as a co-developer of MiddleMan, struggles with the ethics of manipulating public perception to address climate change even as the project spirals in scope with unintended consequences for Ruby's personal life and civilization as a whole. The novel ends with a revelation that recasts the interpretation of many of the computer-styled, unattributed conversations in the book.
